findings.problem: ShardWorkflow has independent status (String), is_validated (bool), and is_sent (bool) fields that can represent impossible combinations like status="pending" with is_sent=true, or status="sent" with is_sent=false and no validated flag.
findings.failure_mode: Any caller can mutate these fields independently, producing shards that are simultaneously marked sent and not validated, or sent with an inconsistent status string. Downstream logic that checks only is_sent without verifying status or is_validated will silently process invalid shards.
findings.fix: Replace status, is_validated, and is_sent with a single ShardStage enum (e.g., Pending, Validated, Sent) and use a fallible constructor or typestate methods to enforce valid transitions. Remove all pub fields.

findings.problem: status is a raw String, not a domain-typed value. Any arbitrary string is accepted as a valid shard status.
findings.failure_mode: Callers can set status to "", null, garbage, or conflicting values. The mark_sent function hardcodes "sent" as a string literal, coupling business logic to a raw string rather than a domain type.
findings.fix: Define a ShardStatus enum with explicit variants (Pending, Validated, Sent) and implement Display/Serialize only for boundary presentation.

findings.problem: is_validated and is_sent are bool lifecycle flags that should be an enum or typestate. Two independent bools encode 4 states but the domain likely has fewer valid states.
findings.failure_mode: The combination (is_validated=false, is_sent=true) is semantically invalid — a shard cannot be sent without being validated. But the type system permits it, and mark_sent does not guard against it.
findings.fix: Replace both bools with a single ShardStage enum or a typestate pattern (e.g., Shard<Pending> -> Shard<Validated> -> Shard<Sent>) where invalid transitions are compile-time errors.

findings.problem: mark_sent takes and returns a owned ShardWorkflow by mutation, directly mutating struct fields. This is imperative shell logic, not a pure calculation. It also lacks a fallible return — there is no typed error for preconditions like not-yet-validated.
findings.failure_mode: No precondition check: mark_sent will set is_sent=true even on a non-validated shard. The caller has no way to handle rejection because the return type is ShardWorkflow, not Result<ShardWorkflow, TransitionError>. Mutation of owned struct fields instead of returning a new value prevents composable, referentially-transparent calls.
findings.fix: Return Result<ShardWorkflow, ShardTransitionError>. Check is_validated before allowing transition to sent. Return the new state value rather than mutating in place.

findings.problem: All struct fields are pub, allowing any caller to bypass all invariants by writing directly to id, status, is_validated, is_sent, or sent_at_epoch_ms.
findings.failure_mode: External crates or modules can set status="hacked" and is_sent=false simultaneously, or clear is_validated after a shard is sent. The type system provides zero protection at the field level.
findings.fix: Make all fields private. Provide accessors (id(), stage(), sent_at()) and mutate only through fallible transition methods on impl ShardWorkflow.

findings.problem: mark_sent uses a hardcoded string literal "sent" for the status field instead of a domain type or constant.
findings.failure_mode: Typos in the string literal produce silently incorrect behavior. Changing the status string requires finding all usages. The string is not validated against a known set of allowed status values.
findings.fix: Replace with a ShardStatus::Sent variant and set status via enum-to-string conversion only at presentation boundaries.

findings.problem: sent_at_epoch_ms is Option<u64> but the type has no domain annotation. There is no constructor enforcing that if is_sent/Sent, then sent_at_epoch_ms must be Some.
findings.failure_mode: A shard can be in Sent state with sent_at_epoch_ms=None, or NonSent state with a timestamp set. No invariant ties the timestamp to the sent state.
findings.fix: Tie sent_at_epoch_ms to the Sent variant of the ShardStage enum or typestate. Use a fallible constructor that rejects Sent without a timestamp.

findings.problem: No benchmarks, profilers, allocation analysis, or second-ring evidence exist for this crate. The crate has no benches/ directory and no benchmark infrastructure.
findings.failure_mode: Performance characteristics of ShardWorkflow allocation (String id copies, ShardWorkflow copies) are unknown. If this type moves frequently through the call stack, the implicit heap allocations for id and status are unmeasured.
findings.fix: Add benches/ with microbenchmarks for ShardWorkflow construction and mark_sent. Profile with cargo-flamegraph or perf to confirm allocation behavior.

residual_risk: Static review only; no commands run. The crate fails multiple Holzman/Rust core contract gates: illegal states are representable, primitive obsession, boolean lifecycle flags, pub fields bypass invariants, no fallible transitions, and hardcoded string literals in domain logic. The type system encodes no domain invariants — this is the highest-risk class of defect in Holzman Rust.
